header.name: Contemporary Studies in Kinship
header.description: This course explores how kinship is imagined, practiced, and contested in contemporary societies. There has been a tendency to assume that with modernity, kinship loses its organizing and explanatory force. However, as this course will demonstrate, kinship remains central to our understanding of contemporary societies. Moving beyond classical anthropological approaches, which privilege static blood/descent-based models grounded in biological givens and ethnocentric bias, this course examines, the 'new turn' in Kinship studies, where on the one hand the heterosexual nuclear family is being brought under the scanner, on the other hand, 'families of choice' and 'intimacies at a distance' are on the rise. None of this is happening in vacuum but is situated within the wider context of shifting demographic processes, economic upheavals, globalised identity movements, transnational mobility, global environmental crisis, technological change and shifting state politics. Drawing on feminist and cultural critique and combining key debates on relatedness, substance, care, and belonging with ethnographic studies, this course will equip learners to question ‘what kinship is and is not’ and understand the  multiple forms and feelings kinship assumes in the contemporary social world.
prerequisites_mandatory: Introduction to Sociology and Anthropology (SOC101)  OR Sociological Theory (SOC210)

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: The course will equip learners to critically analyze classical and contemporary anthropological theories of kinship, assessing their conceptual assumptions and methodological foundations.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Learner will be able to evaluate the contributions of feminist, queer, postcolonial, and cultural critiques to the reconfiguration of kinship studies

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Learners will be able to examine and interpret ethnographic evidence on emerging forms of kinship within broader socio-political and economic contexts.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Learners will be able to develop and articulate original research questions and theoretically informed arguments about contemporary anthropological understandings of kinship as a dynamic and contested field.

lecture_topics: Critiques of Classical Kinship - Feminist and Cultural Critiques
From Kinship to  Relatedness - Substance and Places
Moving Kinship - Migration and Transnational Families
